WAVES / NORMAL MODES / RESONANCE

Standing-wave resonance

Fixed ends, quiet nodes. Tune the drive and watch a string answer.

fₙ = nc/(2L); M = 1/√((1−r²)² + (2ζr)²); r = f/fₙ

LIVE CANVAS
MATHEMATICS, MADE TANGIBLE.Next experiment ↗
A FEW WAYS IN

About this experiment

Drag or tap horizontally across the response graph to tune the drive ratio. Left/right changes the harmonic; up/down changes the drive ratio. Space selects the next harmonic. R restarts the phase. Damping changes resonance height and width; Wave speed changes the natural frequency. P pauses while every control and PNG export remains available. Reduced motion starts paused at a crest. Above three cycles per playback second, motion automatically slows so the wave stays readable; displayed frequencies retain their model values.

The mathematics

A unit-length string is represented by one selected sine mode, sin(nπx). A spatially matched periodic force excites only that mode. The exact steady response has gain M and a phase lag relative to the force; damping ζ keeps resonance finite. The display begins at a response crest, after transients have decayed. The gold points are n + 1 stationary nodes; faint curves show the envelope. The lower graph plots gain against drive ratio on a logarithmic vertical scale. Large amplitudes are visually compressed without changing the gain readout. This is a linear single-mode study, not a general plucked-string or nonlinear stretching solver. Frequencies use normalized time units and no audio is produced.
